title: Coal conveyor, seized idler and belt smouldering
tests: Safety event; tree blames the patrol operator (blame); natural vs forced undecided.
summary: A seized return idler wore through its shell and heated the belt on CV-31 at a coal handling plant. Smoke was seen by the control room and the belt stopped; no flames spread and nobody was hurt. The tree's root cause reads 'patrol operator missed the seized idler'. Thermal scan and idler change history exist but are not linked.

problem.title: Seized idler and belt smouldering on coal conveyor CV-31
problem.site: Coal handling plant, Bowen Basin QLD
problem.whatHappened: On 23 Jun 2026 at about 14:10 the control room saw smoke on CV-31 camera and stopped the belt. A return idler roll near tower 6 was seized, its shell worn through, and the belt underside was scorched over about 2 m. Coal dust around the idler had smouldered. The fire crew dampened the area; no open flame spread.
problem.where: Return idler roll at tower 6, about 90 m from the tail.
problem.when: Daylight, belt running loaded. The idler had been noted as noisy on patrol 4 days earlier.
problem.impact: Belt stopped 9 hours for inspection and idler replacement. Near-miss with fire risk in coal dust. No injury.
problem.duty: Coal from reclaim to the train load-out bin, 1,400 t/h

evidence.title: Seized idler and scorched belt
evidence.note: Shell worn through along one side, bearing housing discoloured, belt underside scorched about 2 m.

evidence.title: Thermal imaging scan results, last 6 months
evidence.note: Quarterly scan of carry idlers only. Return idlers not on the scan route.

evidence.title: Idler change history for CV-31
evidence.note: Most idlers changed on failure. 14 return rolls changed in 12 months, with no planned replacement programme.

evidence.title: Patrol sheet
evidence.note: Noise at tower 6 noted by the operator 4 days before. Sheet has a comments box; no job raised and no priority guide.

evidence.title: Dust build-up along the belt
evidence.note: Coal dust build-up about 100 mm deep on the return frame at towers 5 and 6. Last clean of the belt frame was not recorded.

tree.text: Seized return idler at tower 6 on CV-31 scorched the belt and smouldered

problemDraft.roughNotes: cv31 return idler at tower 6 seized and wore thru the shell. belt scorched under 2m, dust smouldering. control room saw smoke on cam and stopped it. fire crew wet it down. no flames. idler was noisy 4 days ago on patrol and the operator didnt raise a job. rolls in stock. incident report raised.

draft.notes: cv31 return idler at tower 6 seized and wore thru the shell. belt scorched under 2m, dust smouldering. control room saw smoke on cam and stopped it. fire crew wet it down. no flames. idler was noisy 4 days ago on patrol and the operator didnt raise a job. rolls in stock. incident report raised.

mustSuggest.idea: No patrol guide on what to do or how fast for a noisy idler, no priority or severity categories, so no job was raised
Return idlers are not on the thermal scan route
No planned idler replacement or idler condition programme (14 returns changed on failure)
Coal dust build-up at tower 5 and 6 and no housekeeping task on the frame

acceptable: Idler seal design letting dust in
Patrol sheet design (comment box with no action column)
Operators have no way to log from the field
wrongOrDangerous: Operator negligence or lack of attention
Discipline or retraining as the main answer
Adding a patrol without a standard

mustFlag.note: Flagged root with no evidence linked
Bearing failure forced (dust) or natural not decided
No system cause in the tree

mustNotFlag: stopped_at_physical on n1 alone (the human branch exists)
challenge.expectation: Summary says the analysis lands on a person rather than the system; ask what the patrol sheet, thermal route and idler plan did or did not give the operator. Safety: should say the site's incident process comes first.
deliberateWeaknesses: Flagged root n4 blames the operator (blame) and is a hypothesis with no evidence although e4 exists
Action a2 retrains for a system cause (action_weak)
No system cause: thermal scan excludes return idlers (e2), no planned idler replacement (e3), dust build-up (e5)
n2 wear or damage, forced vs natural undecided
No condition monitoring or maintenance task anywhere

capa.deteriorationReasoning: Dust ingress and running an idler to failure are conditions we create. The noise was a warning that the system did not turn into a job. The bearing failure is forced, the fire risk is the dust.
corrective: Replace idler and repair belt (a1 done)
Clean the dust at towers 5 and 6

preventive.what: Patrol standard: what noise or heat gets a job, with priority and a time to action, and a way to raise it from the field
Add return idlers to the thermal scan route and set an alarm temperature rise
preventive.interval: every 3 months, then review from results

preventive.what: Clean coal dust off the return frames and idlers at the towers
Planned idler replacement from the change history (return rolls) rather than run to failure
preventive.interval: starting point to check against the 14 failures in 12 months

preventive.what: Hold return idler rolls and seals at a min level

capa.spares: Return idler rolls and seals for CV-31 type; stock exists, set a minimum.
capa.rollout: All coal conveyors: add return idlers to thermal scan, check dust housekeeping.
unacceptable: Retrain or remind the operator as the only action
Treating it as only an idler failure with no fire risk mention
